answer.generated: When joining many relations, distinct tuples of R must be brought into and out of main memory frequently because the join operation requires comparing tuples across relations, which demands repeated I/O operations to fetch and store data. This approach becomes inefficient due to the high overhead of disk accesses, especially when the relations are large, as each tuple transfer incurs significant latency and bandwidth costs. Thus, the need for constant memory transfers directly contributes to the performance bottleneck of such joins.
